## XRD-PtCoOrdering v2.0.0

A bilingual, offline XRD workspace combining PtCo L1₀ ordering and crystallite-size analysis.

### Download

Download **XRD-PtCoOrdering-v2.0.0.html** from Assets and open it directly in your browser. It is a self-contained application with no installation or network dependency. SHA256SUMS.txt verifies the HTML; the automatically generated Source code archives are optional.

### Changes

- Add the two requested formula modes: (110)/(111) and (110)/[(111)+(200)+(002)], normalized by corresponding reference integrated intensities and reported as **100 × R**. Mode 1 only requires the two relevant peaks.
- Add manual integrated-area entry, traceable reference fields and optional, separately reported calibrated **100 × √R**.
- Correct the single-Gaussian Jacobian parameter order and LM scaling. Add simultaneous Gaussian/linear-background fitting, multiple starts for overlapping (200)/(002), and fit diagnostics/plots. Keep SNIP as an alternative.
- Integrate XRD-Scherrer functionality: single/multi-peak size, FWHM or integral breadth, Gaussian/Cauchy instrument corrections, isotropic Williamson–Hall and independent TEM-calibrated D × C.
- Add Chinese as the default interface with a persistent English switch, shared scan preview and combined CSV/JSON exports. Editing calculation inputs clears affected results.
- Add versioned HTML release attachments and SHA-256 checksums after successful CI validation.

### Validation and interpretation

17 regression groups validate both equations, derivative consistency, fitted areas/widths at different intensity scales, known overlapping peaks, truncated two-peak scans, Scherrer units and corrections, W–H physicality, bilingual behavior and combined exports.

Reference defaults are demonstration values. Supply suitable integrated reference intensities for measured samples. Results above 100% are retained for review. Scherrer returns coherent domain size, not necessarily TEM particle diameter. Kα₂ stripping is not implemented; W–H assumes isolated same-phase reflections and isotropic broadening.
